;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[July 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A [[car bomb]]ing in [[Puli Alam]], [[Logar Province]], kills at least 17 people and injures 30 others. Taliban spokesman [[Zabihullah Mujahid]] says the group has "nothing to do" with the bombing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-53603921 (BBC News)]
**Nine [[Taliban]] militants, including two leaders, are killed by security forces during clashes in [[Ghazni Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/9%C2%A0taliban-killed-attack-afghan-forces-ghazni (TOLOnews)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**A [[car bombing]] attack leaves 5 people dead and another 12 injured in Tel Halef village, [[Syria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-border/car-bomb-kills-at-least-five-near-syrias-ras-al-ain-say-turkeys-anadolu-idUSKCN24V34R (Reuters)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**A bomb kill a soldier in [[Diyala Governorate]], [[Iraq]]. [http://ninanews.com/Website/News/Details?key=846990 (National Iraqi News Agency)]
*A man shoots dead two [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police|policemen]] in [[Charsadda]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1571867/two-police-officials-martyred-in-charsadda-attack (''Dawn'')]

;Business and economy 
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**The [[United States economy]] suffers its worst quarter since [[World War II]], with the [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] shrinking by an annualized rate of 32.9% in the April–June period. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2020/jul/30/us-gdp-economy-worst-quarter-covid-19-unemployment (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Isaias]]
***Hurricane Isaias is expected to head towards [[Florida]], prompting the state to close their [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] sites. The hurricane has made landfall in [[Puerto Rico]], causing landslides, flooding, and power outages. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tropical-storm-isaias-puerto-rico-us-mainland/ (CBS News)] [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2020/07/30/weather/tropical-storm-isaias-forecast-puerto-rico-florida/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Kōriyama explosion]]
**An explosion destroys a restaurant in [[Kōriyama]], [[Japan]], killing one person and injuring another 18. A [[gas leak]] is suspected to be the cause of the accident. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20200730/p2g/00m/0na/050000c (''The Mainichi Shimbun'')]
*[[United States Marine Corps]]
**One Marine is killed and one Sailor and seven additional Marines went missing when their [[Amphibious Assault Vehicle]] sinks near [[San Clemente Island]] off the coast of [[Southern California]].  They were from the [[15th Marine Expeditionary Unit]], stationed at [[Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton]], [[San Diego County]]. This is the third major AAV accident involving Camp Pendleton Marines since 2011.  [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-marine/massive-search-under-way-off-california-for-8-missing-u-s-marines-one-dead-idUSKCN24W1QG (Reuters)] [https://apnews.com/9816c0b6abcf7773f77b6caceb0f7356 (AP)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
*****[[Hong Kong]] reports its largest single day record of 149 new cases of COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours as well as one death. From that new cases, 145 of them are locally transmitted. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthcoronavirus-hongkong/hong-kong-reports-record-daily-number-of-149-new-coronavirus-cases-idUSP8N2BE01N (Reuters)] [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/health-environment/article/3095336/hong-kong-third-wave-city-confirms-fresh-daily (''South China Morning Post'')]
*****Hong Kong government has reversed a day-old total ban on restaurants serving dine-in customers that was introduced to control the spread of COVID-19, and publishes new guidelines that allow restaurants could operate dine-in facilities but only during the day, at 50% capacity, and with no more than two people at a table. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/30/covid-19-hong-kong-drops-ban-on-restaurant-dining-after-one-day (''AFP via The Guardian'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
*****[[Mainland China]] reports 105 new COVID-19 cases and 96 of them are in [[Xinjiang]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-china-cases/mainland-china-reports-105-new-coronavirus-cases-including-96-in-xinjiang-idUSKCN24V05Q (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports 367 new COVID-19 cases. It is the highest jump of new cases since the pandemic began. [http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/13591547 (''Asahi Shimbun'')]
****Japan reports a single day record high of 1,274 new COVID-19 cases. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/07/30/national/tokyos-daily-coronavirus-cases-top-360-thursday-report-says/#.XyLVL1QzbMw (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports its largest single day record of 52,123 new cases of COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/india-sees-daily-record-of-52-000-covid-19-cases/1926917 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record high of 1,197 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/ukraine-sees-record-daily-high-of-1197-new-coronavirus-cases-636868 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record high of 1,356 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.romania-insider.com/coronavirus-cases-jul-30-2020 (Romania Insider)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record high of 615 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours, and authorities warn of a reinstatement of quarantine measures for travellers from other countries. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/poland-reports-its-highest-daily-raise-in-coronavirus-cases/45935958 (Swissinfo)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-poland/poland-may-reimpose-some-curbs-as-daily-covid-19-cases-jump-idUSKCN24V1GN (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
****[[Governor of Wisconsin|Wisconsin Governor]] [[Tony Evers]] issues a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask]] mandate, which is expected to go into effect on August 1. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/wisconsin-governor-orders-masks-statewide-amid-virus-surge-72083164 (ABC News)]
***American businessman and former [[2012 United States presidential election|2012]] [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Herman Cain 2012 presidential campaign|presidential]] candidate [[Herman Cain]] [[List of deaths due to the COVID-19 pandemic|dies]] from complications of [[COVID-19]] at age 74. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/tommybeer/2020/07/30/former-presidential-candidate-herman-cain-dies-from-coronavirus-at-74/ (''Forbes'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/former-gop-presidential-candidate-herman-cain-dead-coronavirus-n1235312 (NBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] records 723 new cases, as well as 13 deaths. It is the highest jump of number of cases and deadliest day since the start of the pandemic in Australia. [https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/victoria-records-723-new-coronavirus-cases-13-deaths-on-state-s-deadliest-day-20200730-p55gvk.html (''The Age'')]
***[[New South Wales]] reports its first COVID-19 cases from prison inmates as the state reports 18 new cases. [https://www.smh.com.au/national/nsw/sydney-coronavirus-cluster-grows-as-nsw-records-first-case-in-prison-inmate-20200730-p55gv5.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[First Lady of Brazil|First Lady]] [[Michelle Bolsonaro]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/07/30/897196730/michelle-bolsonaro-brazils-first-lady-tests-positive-for-coronavirus (NPR)]
**The number of worldwide recoveries of COVID-19 surpasses ten million. [https://gisanddata.maps.arcgis.com/apps/opsdashboard/index.html#/bda7594740fd40299423467b48e9ecf6 (Johns Hopkins University)]

;International relations
*[[Malaysia–Philippines relations]], [[North Borneo dispute]]
**[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Malaysia)|Malaysian Foreign Minister]] [[Hishammuddin Hussein]] summons the Philippine [[ambassador]] after [[Department of Foreign Affairs (Philippines)|Philippine Foreign Secretary]] [[Teodoro Locsin Jr.]] tweeted Monday to the [[Embassy of the United States, Manila|U.S. embassy in Manila]] that [[Sabah]] does not belong to [[Malaysia]]. Locsin summons the Malaysian ambassador in tit-for-tat. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/malaysia-philippines-war-words-sabah-claim-200730032257250.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Agbudu shooting]]
**A [[mass shooting]] in [[Kogi State]], [[Nigeria]] leaves 14 people dead and another six injured. Thirteen of the fatalities were member of the same family. Police said that a long-standing row over land rights is suspected to be the motive behind the attack. [https://guardian.ng/news/gunmen-kill-family-of-13-in-kogi-state/ (''The Guardian Nigeria'')]
*[[Shooting of Michael Brown]]
**[[St. Louis County, Missouri|St. Louis County]] prosecutor [[Wesley Bell]] announces that Darren Wilson, the [[Ferguson Police Department (Missouri)|Ferguson police]] officer that shot and killed Michael Brown, will not be charged. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/30/us/michael-brown-darren-wilson-ferguson.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Twelve people are dead and nine others injured during a [[mass shooting]] in the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]], carried out by a drunk [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|soldier]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-crime/congo-soldier-shoots-dead-12-in-drunken-rampage-idUSKCN24W1Y7 (Reuters)]
*Former [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] Trevor Reed, a 29-year-old student, is sentenced for nine years in a Russian penal colony for assaulting two [[Police of Russia|police]] officers while drunk last year in [[Moscow]]. Reed's father told reporters after the verdict he is planning to appeal directly to [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/russia-jails-marine-trevor-reed-police-assault-200730104547653.html (Al Jazeera)]
*A court in [[Uganda]] sentences a [[Poaching|poacher]] who killed a rare gorilla named Rafiki to 11 years in prison. Rafiki, a 25-year-old [[silverback]] who was the head of a gorilla group in the southwestern [[Bwindi Impenetrable Forest National Park]], was killed with a spear in early June. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/uganda-poacher-killed-rare-gorilla-11-years-jail-200730112507761.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Hong Kong legislative election]]
**At least 12 [[Hong Kong]] pro-democracy nominees for the September election are disqualified, among them, [[Dennis Kwok]], [[Joshua Wong]], [[Tiffany Yuen]], and three others from the [[Civic Party]]. Other nominations were still being reviewed, the government said in a statement expressing support for the disqualifications. [https://apnews.com/8f496468b3b0c2ac87bb5b466f6d8180 (AP)]
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] has suggested [[2020 United States presidential election|November's presidential election]] could be postponed, saying increased [[postal voting]] could lead to fraud and inaccurate results. Under the [[Constitution of the United States|U.S. Constitution]], Trump does not have the authority to [[United States presidential election|postpone the election]] himself; a delay would have to be approved by both houses of Congress. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53597975 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Exploration of Mars]]
**The [[Mars 2020]] mission carrying the [[Perseverance (rover)|''Perseverance'' rover]] and Mars helicopter ''[[Mars Helicopter Ingenuity|Ingenuity]]'' successfully launches atop an [[Atlas V]] rocket from [[Cape Canaveral Space Launch Complex 41|Cape Canaveral SLC-41]]. [https://www.space.com/news/live/mars-perseverance-rover-updates (Space.com)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2019–20 NBA season]]
***The [[National Basketball Association]] season resumes at the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] after a 141-day [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|suspension]] due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The season resumes with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] taking on the [[Utah Jazz]]. [https://people.com/sports/the-nba-season-returns-tonight-after-a-141-day-hiatus-heres-how-to-watch/?amp=true (''People'')] [https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pelicans-vs-jazz-score-live-updates-as-nba-season-restarts-from-disney-bubble-zion-williamson-good-to-go/live/ (CBS Sports)]
*A [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-backed consortium ends its bid to purchase [[Premier League]] team [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. The takeover bid was stalled due to concerns about [[Human rights in Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia's human rights record]] and the Kingdom's promotion of the [[Pirate television|pirate]] TV station [[beoutQ]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/saudi-bid-buy-newcastle-ends-piracy-human-rights-issues-200730151208845.html (Al Jazeera)]
